title: Close a used needle's safety guard one-handed against a fixed block, then put the syringe in the sharps container
instruction: Close the safety guard over the used needle, then put the syringe in the sharps container.
context: Phlebotomists, medical and dental assistants (O*NET 31-9097.00, 31-9092.00, 31-9091.00) close a safety needle's hinged guard right after use with the hand holding it, pressing it on a hard surface so the free hand never nears the point (OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030). The rule is unstated. Unlike TK-4ZTXQ4 (pick a sharps bin), TK-TBHCWS (blood-draw step order) and our TK-MS2APD (retract a blade), this task scores the method: one hand, against a fixed surface.
setup: Positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: 'in front' is away from the arms, 'right' is the robot's right; heights are above the table top. Tray (fixed, dark blue plastic): inside 240 x 160 mm, 4 mm floor, 4 mm rim 15 mm above the floor; inside spans 22.0 to 46.0 cm in front and 8.5 to 24.5 cm right of the midline. On its floor: an activation block (fixed, light grey, 20 x 20 x 50 mm tall) at 38.0 to 40.0 cm in front and 13.0 to 15.0 cm right; and two pairs of grey ridges (each ridge 10 mm long, 4 mm wide, 11 mm tall, a pair 8 mm apart inside), 20.0 cm right, at 28.0 and 34.0 cm in front. Syringe (loose, 40 g including its 10 g guard) lying on the ridges, needle pointing away from the robot: clear barrel 18 mm across and 90 mm long, its middle 31.0 cm in front and 20.0 cm right; at its back end a clear finger flange 12 mm wide and 38 mm tall (wings up and down, the lower one on the tray floor), a white plunger rod and 16 mm thumb press; at its front an orange 10 mm hub and a steel needle 6 mm across and 40 mm long (tip 40.5 cm in front). The orange safety guard (10 x 46 x 10 mm) is hinged at the hub on an upright axis and points to the robot's left, square to the needle; swung 90 deg toward the tip it lies along the needle, its end 3 mm past the tip. A light spring holds it open; within 4 deg of closed it clicks and stays shut. Sharps container (fixed, yellow, red side toward the robot's right): inside 220 x 90 mm and 86 mm deep (90 mm tall, 4 mm walls and floor), centred 30.0 cm in front on the midline. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged over the whole trial from the video and a top photo. The guard closes against a surface when, from the moment it is 30 deg round from open until it clicks, its outer half always touches a fixed surface (block, tray or container, within 3 mm), no gripper finger comes within 20 mm of the guard's centre line, and the syringe is over the tray. Closed: clicked and within 10 deg of lying along the needle. Released: every gripper's finger tips more than 5 mm above the syringe's top, or more than 15 mm plus half the finger opening from its outline seen from above. Still: under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s. 1.0: closed against a surface, the syringe released and still in the container (all of it inside the walls seen from above, below the rim, lowest point within 1.5 mm of the floor). 0.5: the same but on the tray (lowest point within 1.5 mm of its floor). 0 otherwise, and 0 for the whole trial once the guard has closed any other way, or the syringe has been within 2 mm of the table outside the tray and container. Scored at the last step, or 1.0 once held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Swing the guard back open (it releases from its click), lay the syringe back on the ridges with the flange wings up and down and the guard pointing to the robot's left. The tray, block and container are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate, about twice real size, rigid boxes and cylinders with the simulator's default friction. Real hinged guards fold down over the needle and are usually pressed onto the table top; here the guard swings flat on an upright hinge so a straight-down grip can work it. The click is simulated: a 0.02 N m/rad spring holds the guard open, then shut once within 4 deg of closed. The needle is 6 mm thick. The syringe rests turned about 20 deg about its axis on the ridges.
